findings.text: the reviewed run's manifest records its gate commands as templates rather than literal commands: the tests field spells the invocation with <worktree> placeholders and the baseline_suite and after_suite command fields end with '<the 57 files listed in logs/baseline-population.log>' rather than the literal argv. justifications.durability: the seven assertions are real regression guards, not vacuous: at base b65b7c6da they fail (7 failed, EXIT=1) and at head they pass, and each is exercised from inside an unrelated git repository whose facts are adversarial (its head is both the recorded base and the cited commit, or the declared file is dirty), so a reader that fell back to the working directory answers with those facts and fails. The guard does not extend to the three remaining readers in recovery.py and dispatch.py, which stay reachable with a blank field.

Weakness: the reviewed manifest's tests, baseline_suite and after_suite fields carry unsubstituted angle-bracket placeholders (<worktree>, <the 57 files listed in logs/...>) instead of the literal commands, so the manifest alone does not carry its own reproduction receipt; the literal commands survive only in the logs' header lines. This is the finding below and the reason evidence is not higher.

No plan, sprint or ticket label and no author attribution appears in the added code, tests or fragment - a scan of the commit's added lines for section/phase/ticket tokens finds none - and the comment/helper placement follows the file's existing idiom.

Those three are outside this commit's promotion.py write scope and the node reported them under follow_ons rather than silently, which is why the deduction is 3 rather than larger.
